Start here - all four modes

Prepare the receptor once

The receptor preparation panel now sits above the Single Dock, Batch Dock, Co-Dock and Redock tabs. All modes reuse its receptor and docking box.

  1. Open https://anyone-docking.streamlit.app/. In Step 1 - Shared receptor preparation, keep Download from RCSB and enter 1M17. Press Enter or click outside the field to commit it. ACD tries mmCIF first and falls back to PDB if necessary.
  2. Keep Auto-detect co-crystal ligand for this example. Open Receptor setup panel to review the selected co-crystal ligand and which waters, metal ions, cofactors or lipids are retained. A full mmCIF ligand identifier must not be shortened to a three-character code.
  3. Keep the X, Y and Z search-box sizes at 18 A for this example. Inspect the pocket rather than assuming the example box suits every target. Manual XYZ and ProDy selection are alternatives; Blind docking instead covers the supplied protein.
  4. Review missing-residue warnings. Choose a suitable complete structure or repair and validate missing regions near the pocket before scientific use. For this first tutorial run, leave flexible side chains off. Optional side-chain flexibility is selected here, not separately inside each mode.
  5. Click Prepare Receptor. Wait for Receptor ready and inspect 3D: Receptor + Docking Box. In the captured example the selected reference is AQ4_A_999, the center is (22.01, 0.25, 52.79) A and the box is 18 x 18 x 18 A.
  6. Leave Replicate seeds (1 = off) at 1 for this shared-server tutorial. Now choose a docking-mode tab. If you change the receptor, reference ligand, box or flexible-residue selection, prepare the receptor again.
One prepared receptor, four different tasks. Switching mode tabs is not the same as preparing a new receptor. Do not ignore structure-quality warnings simply because the Run button is enabled.

One ligand - erlotinib

Single Dock: prepare one ligand and inspect its poses

Use the shared 1M17 receptor and search for erlotinib. Ligand preparation, docking and results remain within the Single Dock tab.

  1. Select Single Dock. Under Ligand Preparation, keep PubChem / SMILES. Type erlotinib into Compound name and click Search. Check the returned compound information and SMILES; a name search is not a guarantee of the intended stereochemistry or salt form.
  2. Set Output name to erlotinib and Target pH to 7.4. Keep pKaNET Cloud+ and click Prepare Ligand. Wait for Ligand ready. Review the final SMILES, formal charge and ranked microstates; merely inspecting a candidate must not be confused with changing the docking input.
  3. In Run Docking keep Exhaustiveness 8, Number of poses 10 and Energy range 3 kcal/mol. Ten is a requested maximum, not a guarantee that ten distinct poses will be returned. The public-app replicate setting remains 1.
  4. For the plain Single Dock example, leave Dock co-crystal ligand as reference off; the dedicated Redock walkthrough below shows validation separately. Click Run Docking once and wait. Typically 2-6 min; actual runtime depends on system size, sampling parameters and current server load.
  5. In Results & Visualization inspect the score table, pose selector and 3D pocket. In this captured run, pose 1 scored -7.11 kcal/mol with 7.83 A RMSD from the crystal: do not present this as successful crystal-pose reproduction. Cyan identifies the docked ligand; magenta/pink identifies the crystal reference where displayed. Inspect alternative poses rather than accepting the first pose uncritically.
  6. Below the 3D result, open 2D Interaction Diagrams. Generate the ACD, RDKit or ProLIF diagram as needed; PoseView uses an external service and may not be available. Check that the diagram, pose label, affinity and RMSD refer to the same selected pose. Download the desired structures and scores.

Three separate ligands - name search

Batch Dock: aspirin, baicalein and caffeine

Build the batch through Compound name search, one compound at a time. Do not paste three names into one search field.

  1. Select Batch Dock, then choose Compound name in Input mode. The shared receptor and box prepared above are reused.
  2. Type aspirin into Compound name and click Search. Review the PubChem hit. Confirm that one SMILES entry has been added to the editable list.
  3. Replace the search text with baicalein and click Search. Check the returned structure and confirm a second line has been appended; do not replace the aspirin line.
  4. Replace the search text with caffeine and click Search. Confirm that the editable list now contains three entries: aspirin, baicalein and caffeine. The application may initially use systematic names; review and rename only the name after each SMILES if shorter labels are needed. Do not change the SMILES accidentally.
  5. Keep Target pH 7.4 and pKaNET Cloud+ for the teaching example. Uncheck Dock co-crystal ligand as reference for this three-compound run; the dedicated Redock walkthrough is performed separately. When enabled, that checkbox adds an automatic co-crystal reference run, not a fourth compound you need to search for.
  6. Keep Exhaustiveness 8, Poses per ligand 10 and Energy range 3 kcal/mol. Click Run Batch Docking once. Each entered ligand is prepared and docked independently against the same receptor; this is not simultaneous co-binding.
  7. Inspect Batch Results and select a ligand and pose for the 3D and 2D viewers. Compare results only under matching preparation and docking conditions. Click Generate ProLIF Barcode to show Interaction Profile Table and save CSV, PNG or SVG. Download the batch results.
  8. Read the interaction matrix as ligand rows and the union of interacting receptor residues as columns, with duplicate residue columns merged. White means no detected interaction; colors identify the classes in the legend. This batch profile uses pose 1 of each ligand, not an average across every returned pose. If optional reference redocking is enabled, a separate minimum-RMSD reference row can also be included.
This is an interface demonstration, not a claim that aspirin, baicalein or caffeine is an experimentally validated binder of 1M17. A docking score alone cannot establish that claim.

Two ligands in one joint search - benzene + methanol

Co-Dock: benzene and methanol together

Co-Dock is different from Batch Dock: every joint pose contains one copy of each input ligand, and the score describes the combined pose.

  1. Select Co-Dock. Confirm the notice that the shared receptor and docking box are being used.
  2. Choose Compound name, search benzene, and review the returned structure and the appended SMILES line.
  3. Replace the Compound name search text with methanol and click Search. Confirm that the editable list contains exactly two entries: benzene (C1=CC=CC=C1, equivalently c1ccccc1) and methanol (CO). Methanol is CH3OH, not a methyl radical. Do not replace the benzene entry when adding methanol.
  4. Keep two ligands for this demonstration. The interface accepts 2-4 ligands. Keep pH 7.4, Exhaustiveness 8, Combined poses 10 and Energy range 3 kcal/mol. Review Keep input charge state rather than changing it without a chemical reason.
  5. Click Run Co-Dock and wait for Done - joint docking complete. In Co-Dock results select View combined pose and confirm that both ligands are present. In this viewer benzene is cyan and methanol is magenta; magenta here means the second co-docked ligand, not the crystal reference used in the other modes. A joint score is not a separate binding affinity for either component and must not be compared directly with Batch Dock scores. This workflow does not enumerate all ligand pairings or subsets.
  6. Download the joint docking output and record the input ligands, shared receptor, box and parameters. Treat a small-molecule toy example as a UI demonstration, not proof of co-binding or cooperativity.
Benzene and methanol are a simple interface demonstration. They are separate input molecules, not a covalently linked product, and their combined docking score is not evidence of biological co-binding or cooperativity.

Crystal-pose validation - no manual SMILES

Redock the selected co-crystal ligand

The dedicated Redock tab uses the crystal reference selected during shared receptor preparation. There is no separate manual ligand-SMILES input.

  1. Select Redock. Confirm Using the shared receptor, box, and selected crystal reference ligand. Expand Reference ligand contacts and missing-residue assessment and review the reference and pocket quality.
  2. Keep pH 7.4, Protonation mode pkanet, Exhaustiveness 8, Maximum poses 10 and Energy range 3 kcal/mol for this example. The extracted co-crystal ligand is prepared automatically; do not enter erlotinib SMILES in the Single Dock tab to make Redock work.
  3. Click Redock once. Wait for ligand preparation, Vina docking and RMSD calculation to finish. If structure-quality checks block the run, choose or repair the structure rather than bypassing the check.
  4. In Pose Browser inspect the affinity and crystal RMSD columns. Poses are ordered by lowest crystal RMSD, with the original Vina pose numbers retained. In the captured run the first RMSD-ranked result is Vina pose 6: 1.30 A RMSD and -6.88 kcal/mol. It is not necessarily Vina pose 1 or the best-scored pose.
  5. Use Pose (RMSD order) to change the selected pose and compare the cyan docked ligand with the magenta/pink crystal ligand in 3D. The same selected pose drives the 2D Interaction Diagrams immediately below the viewer.
  6. Generate the selected pose's 2D diagram and inspect the reference comparison. Download the selected SDF/PDB, RMSD-ranked scores CSV and original crystal reference. Report unavailable RMSD as unavailable: the existing 60% common-substructure coverage gate must pass before RMSD is interpreted.
Low RMSD supports reproduction of this crystal pose under these conditions; it does not prove general predictive accuracy or measured affinity. Distinguish pose sampling from score ranking, and report the seed and preparation choices.

Interpret with care

  • Docking scores are model predictions, not experimentally measured binding affinities. These tutorial compounds are teaching examples, not validated activity claims.
  • Missing residues or unresolved atoms near the binding pocket can change its geometry. Repair and validate the structure, or select a suitable alternative.
  • Default rigid docking keeps receptor side chains fixed. Optional selected side-chain flexibility does not make the entire receptor flexible.
  • Protonation, tautomerism, stereochemistry, waters, cofactors, metals and heme can affect results. Review the actual prepared species and receptor contents.
  • Vina does not score metal-coordination geometry. Treat reported metal proximities as distance-based contacts, not validated coordination bonds; follow short-contact warnings.
  • A good minimum RMSD with a poor top-scored RMSD can indicate a ranking problem rather than insufficient sampling. Increasing exhaustiveness is not a guaranteed solution.
  • RMSD is unavailable when the existing 60% common-substructure coverage gate fails. Do not replace unavailable values with zero.
  • Shared-server resources and external services can delay or limit jobs. Download important results; a browser session is not durable archival storage.
  • RCSB and PubChem fetch public data; PoseView uses an external service. Review privacy implications before submitting confidential structures to hosted workflows or third-party services.
Screenshots document the interface and examples observed on the capture date. Scores and poses vary between runs. These teaching examples are not evidence of biological activity. Project source.
